requirement:
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.test-coverage.index`. The only obligations are the two MUSTs; the MAY imposes nothing to check.

**Obligation 1: reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside Markdown code examples.**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[marker_ranges]` finds `{coverage-index}` colon fences. It uses `colon_fence`, which needs at least three colons.
- It skips fences that overlap `protected_ranges` (`src/lib.rs`). Those ranges come from the pulldown-cmark parser and cover code blocks, inline code and HTML.
- It returns an error for a directive with arguments, for a missing closing fence of at least the opening length, and for a nonempty body.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate_in]` collects the ranges from every chapter. It errors with "only one {coverage-index} directive is permitted" if more than one is found. `populate` calls `populate_in`.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[directive_fences_and_markdown_examples]` is marked `{test}`. It covers each case:
  - A directive inside a fenced code block gives 0 ranges.
  - A longer closing fence is accepted.
  - An unclosed directive, a nonempty body and arguments are each rejected.
  - Two directives in two chapters make `populate` fail with "only one".

**Obligation 2: when the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` replaces it with the summary report.**
- `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` calls `execution_coverage::populate`.
- `populate_in` builds the summary and calls `chapter.content.replace_range(range, &summary)` on the index chapter. It also appends the detail chapters.
- If no directive is found, it returns `Ok(())` and does nothing.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` is marked `{test}`. It asserts that the rendered chapter contains the coverage figures and no longer contains `{coverage-index}`.

The content of the report belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`, which is cited context here. I did not reassess it.

**Unspecified behavior.** None of the behavior beyond the text is a gap. The chapter-path requirement and the report-path conflict errors are generated-page concerns. `populate` also carries `{impl}` references to the other index requirements.

text: :::{req} index
A book MAY contain one standalone `{coverage-index}` directive with an empty
body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. The
preprocessor MUST reject duplicate, unclosed, or nonempty directives outside
Markdown code examples. When the directive is present, `habeas mdbook` MUST
replace it with the report of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
